Looking at the verification errors, I need to analyze the logic more carefully:

1. The forall statement's postcondition isn't being satisfied
2. The assertion `merged[q] == m[q]` might not hold

The key insight is that in `K.Override(m,n)`, when `q in n`, the value is `n[q]`, not `m[q]`. So the logic for determining which value to use needs to check `q in n` first, not `q in m`.

Let me trace through the logic:
- `merged = K.Override(m,n)` means for any `q in merged`: value is `n[q]` if `q in n`, else `m[q]`
- `left = K.Restrict(merged, keep)` - restricts merged to keys in keep
- `rm = K.Restrict(m, keep)`, `rn = K.Restrict(n, keep)`
- `right = K.Override(rm, rn)` - for any `q in right`: value is `rn[q]` if `q in rn`, else `rm[q]`

For `q in left`:
- `q in merged` and `q in keep`
- `left[q] == merged[q]` (from RestrictAt)
- `merged[q] == (if q in n then n[q] else m[q])` (from OverrideAt)

For `right[q]`:
- `right[q] == (if q in rn then rn[q] else rm[q])`
- If `q in n` and `q in keep`, then `q in rn` and `rn[q] == n[q]`
- If `q not in n` but `q in m` and `q in keep`, then `q in rm` and `rm[q] == m[q]`

So I need to check `q in n` first, then handle the case where `q in m` (but not in n).

```json
{
  "HelperA.dfy": "var merged := K.Override(m,n);\n    var left := K.Restrict(merged,keep);\n    var rm := K.Restrict(m,keep);\n    var rn := K.Restrict(n,keep);\n    var right := K.Override(rm,rn);\n    D.OverrideKeys(m,n);\n    D.RestrictKeys(merged,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(m,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(n,keep);\n    D.OverrideKeys(rm,rn);\n    assert left.Keys == right.Keys;\n    forall q | q in left ensures q in right && left[q] == right[q] {\n      V.RestrictAt(merged,keep,q);\n      V.OverrideAt(m,n,q);\n      V.OverrideAt(rm,rn,q);\n      if q in n {\n        V.RestrictAt(n,keep,q);\n      } else {\n        V.RestrictAt(m,keep,q);\n      }\n    }\n    A.Equal(left,right);"
}
```
